For simplicity's sake I will only talk about Fallout 3 and Fallout: New Vegas here. They're very much connected to the first two games, but those are completely different, isometric, turn-based RPGs that are a bit rough to gent into nowadays. No harm in giving them a shot, but they're a completely different beast and given the choice between Fallout and Bioshock, I'll assume you're limiting yourself to FO3 and FNV, as those are the only Fallouts remotely comparable to Bioshock (namely they're all FPSes).

That said, the Fallouts will net you a lot more game time. Between the base games and DLCs you can easily log 100 hours into each game. They're open world games with tons of stuff to do, the Bioshocks are much more linear and limited in that regard.

That said, Bioshock 1 and Bioshock Infinite (I haven't ever played Bioshock 2 so I can't comment on that, but I'd definitely recommend playing 1 and Infinite given the choice) are extremely polished experiences. The gameplay is mostly fun and solid, if nothing out of the ordinary, and not nearly as deep as the Fallouts'. Length-wise you're very, very likely to spend a lot less on each one than either of the Fallouts, for a completionist run we're probably talking some 15-20 hours for each I'd say.

The Fallouts are basically RPGs first and foremost, lots of stuff to do, lots of room to freeroam and dick around.

The Bioshocks are about the story and atmosphere first and foremost, and the story is excellent, in both games. I personally think that the story of BS:I is one of the most creative and incredible things ever written for, and presented in, a video game.

I would recommend playing all four games at some point, they're all incredible games, but it's hard to recommend which one to play immediately or which one to start out with.

As for the order, I'd play FO3 before NV and BS1 before BS:I, but whether you start with Fallout or Bioshock really depends on what you're in for right now I suppose.

EDIT: As for how connected they are; The games are connected in that they play in the same universe (well, actually it's a bit more complicated with BS:I but I won't go into that :)) but they're mostly independent storylines, so you require no knowledge of previous games to enjoy either. I'd still play FO3 before NV and BS1 before BS:I though because that's the release order and gameplay improvements as well as shout-outs to previous titles make the games more enjoyable when played in that order.

As far as Fallout 3 vs. Fallout NV are concerned:

Fallout 3 is more sophisticated in terms of its exploration. It explains the setting better, comes with a wide variety of interesting revelations. In terms of level design it is much more complex since it features large urban areas with vast underground networks and tons of well known landmarks.

Fallout NV is more sophisticated in terms of its character development, both in regards to mechanical build options as well as what choices and alliances you make throughout the game. It features many more factions and nuanced choices. Your character is also more of a blank slate.
